prompt: Draw the architecture of our web app: browsers talk to a load balancer, which spreads traffic over two app servers (group them as the app tier), and both servers use one database.

checks.why: the database drawn as a database (cylinder)
the two app servers grouped in an app tier

expect.$expr: (() => { const g = v.groups.find((x) => /app/i.test(x.label)); return !!g && v.nodes.filter((n) => n.parentId === g.id).length === 2; })()

checks.why: the load balancer reaches both servers, and both reach the database

expect.$expr: (() => { const lb = v.nodes.find((n) => /balanc/i.test(n.label)); const db = v.nodes.find((n) => ['cyl', 'h-cyl', 'lin-cyl'].includes(n.shape)); const g = v.groups.find((x) => /app/i.test(x.label)); const servers = v.nodes.filter((n) => n.parentId === g.id); return servers.every((s) => v.edges.some((e) => e.source === lb.id && e.target === s.id) && v.edges.some((e) => e.source === s.id && e.target === db.id)); })()

args.source:
flowchart LR
  browser[Browser] -->|HTTPS| lb[Load balancer]
  subgraph app [App tier]
    app1[App server 1]
    app2[App server 2]
  end
  lb --> app1
  lb --> app2
  app1 -->|SQL| db[(Database)]
  app2 -->|SQL| db
